cues.caption: Welcome back, champ!
cues.text: Hey champ, welcome back! It's so good to see you again.

cues.caption: Last time: Loops · repeat 5 times: clap
cues.text: Last time, you learned about loops. Instead of saying clap, clap, clap, clap, clap, we just said, repeat five times, clap. So smart!

cues.caption: Chapter 4 · If This, Then That
cues.text: Today is chapter four of Unit two, Thinking Like a Computer. And it's called, If This, Then That.

cues.caption: Today: Robo learns to make choices!
cues.text: So far, Robo just follows steps, one after another. But today, Robo learns something new. How to make a choice! Ready?

cues.caption: Monday morning. Aarav is ready for school
cues.text: Let me tell you about Aarav. It's Monday morning, and Aarav is getting ready for school. Bag packed. Tiffin packed. Shoes on.

cues.caption: Should Aarav take the umbrella?
cues.text: Near the door, there's an umbrella. Should Aarav take it with him? What do you think?

cues.caption: It depends! First, he checks the weather
cues.text: Hmm. The answer is, it depends! It depends on the weather. So before he decides, Aarav does something clever. He looks out of the window, and checks.

cues.caption: If it rains, then take an umbrella
cues.text: Dark clouds, and pitter patter, it's raining! So Aarav grabs the umbrella. If it rains, then take an umbrella. That's a rule!

cues.caption: IF something is true → THEN do this
cues.text: Rules like this have a special shape. If, something is true, then, do something. We call it an if then rule.

cues.caption: Condition = the thing you check · true or not
cues.text: The part after if is called the condition. A condition is the thing you check. Like, is it raining? The answer can only be yes, it's true, or no, it's not true.

cues.caption: THEN happens only when the condition is true
cues.text: The part after then is the action. And here's the important bit. The then part only happens when the condition is true. No rain? No umbrella!

cues.caption: What about a sunny day?
cues.text: But wait. What about a sunny day? What should Aarav do then?

cues.caption: ELSE = otherwise · leave the umbrella at home
cues.text: For that, we add one more little word. Else. Else means, otherwise. Do the other thing. If it rains, then take an umbrella. Else, leave the umbrella at home. Now, rain or shine, Aarav always knows what to do.

cues.caption: A branch: one way OR the other, never both
cues.text: Think of it like a fork in the road. The steps come to the condition, and then go one way, or the other way. Never both! This fork is called a branch.

cues.caption: Raju bhaiya checks the traffic light
cues.text: Now, let's hop into an auto rickshaw! Our driver, Raju bhaiya, comes to a traffic signal. What does he do first? He checks the light.

cues.caption: If red → stop. Else → go carefully
cues.text: His rule is simple. If the light is red, then stop. Else, go carefully. He checks the light every single time, before he decides.

cues.caption: The light is green. Stop or go?
cues.text: Now, the light turns green. Should Raju bhaiya stop, or go? Think about it.

cues.caption: Green is not red → the ELSE part: go!
cues.text: Go! Green is not red, so the condition is not true. That means the else part happens. Off we go, carefully. Beep beep!

cues.caption: If Aarav is hungry, then he eats his tiffin
cues.text: If then rules hide inside stories too. At lunch time, if Aarav is hungry, then he eats his tiffin. Yum!

cues.caption: If the bell rings, then go to class
cues.text: Suddenly, ring ring! If the bell rings, then go to class. The bell just rang, so the condition is true. So what does Aarav do? He does the then part, and goes to class!

cues.caption: Homework done? Cricket! Else, homework first
cues.text: In the evening, his friends call him to play cricket. But Aarav's mum has a rule. If homework is done, then play cricket. Else, finish homework first! See how the else gives Aarav a sensible other choice? That's fair, isn't it?

cues.caption: Which one is an if-then rule?
cues.text: Quick game! Only one of these is an if then rule. I like mangoes. The sky is blue. Chai is hot. If I'm hungry, then I eat my tiffin. Which one is it?

cues.caption: It checks something, then says what to do
cues.text: If I'm hungry, then I eat my tiffin! It checks something, am I hungry, and then it says what to do. The others are just facts. They don't check anything.

cues.caption: If I'm sleepy, then ___. Else ___.
cues.text: Now, let's make our own rule, for bedtime! If I'm sleepy, then, what? And else, what? Think of your own answer.

cues.caption: Then: go to bed. Else: read one more story
cues.text: Here's mine. If I'm sleepy, then I go to bed. Else, I read one more story. Yours can be different, and that's totally okay!

cues.caption: Game characters follow if-then rules too!
cues.text: Now here's where computers come in. Video game characters follow if then rules all the time!

cues.caption: If lives = 0 → Game over. Else → keep playing
cues.text: In lots of games, you have lives, shown as little hearts. When all the hearts are gone, you have zero lives. So the game has a rule. If lives equals zero, then, game over. Else, keep playing.

cues.caption: The game checks the rule again and again
cues.text: The game checks this rule again and again, every time something happens. Bump! One life gone. Check. Still not zero? Keep playing!

cues.caption: 2 lives left. Game over, or keep playing?
cues.text: So, your character has two lives left. What happens? Game over, or keep playing?

cues.caption: 2 is not 0 → else → keep playing!
cues.text: Keep playing! Two is not zero, so the condition isn't true, and the else part runs. Phew!

cues.caption: Your turn: practice check
cues.text: Okay champ, practice time! Here's a check, just like the quiz.

cues.caption: If the light is red, then ___. Else ___.
cues.text: Fill in the blanks. If the light is red, then, blank. Else, blank. You can pause the video, and try it on paper.

cues.caption: If red, then stop. Else, go carefully.
cues.text: Here's one answer. If the light is red, then stop. Else, go carefully. Did you get it? Brilliant! You just wrote your own if then else rule.

cues.caption: IF = check a condition
cues.text: Let's remember what we learned. If means, check a condition. Like, is it raining?

cues.caption: THEN = what to do if it's true
cues.text: Then is what to do when the condition is true. Only then!

cues.caption: ELSE = what to do if it's not
cues.text: Else is what to do when it's not true. Otherwise, do the other thing.

cues.caption: Red light → stop. Else → go
cues.text: And at the signal? Red light, stop. Else, go!

cues.caption: Chapter 4 done!
cues.text: Chapter four, done! Now you can make choices, just like a computer. Super work, champ!

cues.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
cues.text: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
